review_status: REVIEWED — every row carries the decision that kept it

source_upgrades.pappg_ps_overview: The overview includes a description of the activity that would result if the proposal were funded and a statement of objectives and methods to be employed.
source_upgrades.pappg_ps_merit: The statement on intellectual merit should describe the potential of the proposed activity to advance knowledge.
source_upgrades.pappg_ps_impacts: The statement on broader impacts should describe the potential of the proposed activity to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.

rules.label: Omit page numbers from uploaded files

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: Each section of the proposal that is uploaded as a file should leave out page numbering unless otherwise directed within Research.gov.
rules.why: System auto-pagination ensures consistent formatting across the entire proposal package without conflicting page numbers.

rules.label: Use approved fonts and sizes

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: Use one of the following fonts identified below: • Arial7 (not Arial Narrow), Courier New, or Palatino Linotype at a font size of 10 points or larger; • Times New Roman at a font size of 11 points or larger; or • Computer Modern family of fonts at a font size of 11 points or larger.
rules.why: Standard fonts and minimum sizes ensure legibility for reviewers and prevent unfair space advantages.

rules.label: Restrict reduced font sizes to allowed exceptions

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: A font size of less than 10 points may be used for mathematical formulas or equations, figures, tables, or diagram captions and when using a Symbol font to insert Greek letters or special characters.
rules.why: Allows compact formatting for complex technical elements while preserving general text legibility.

rules.label: Observe line spacing limit

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: No more than six lines of text within a vertical space of one inch.
rules.why: Prevents dense text packing that creates unfair length advantages and reduces reviewer readability.

rules.label: Maintain one-inch margins

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: Margins, in all directions, must be at least an inch.
rules.why: Ensures uniform printable margins and clean layout for electronic document rendering.

rules.label: Exclude content from page margins

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: No proposer-supplied information may appear in the margins.
rules.why: Prevents applicants from bypassing page limits by placing text or headers in the margin space.

rules.label: Use standard letter paper size

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: Paper size must be no larger than standard letter paper size (8½ by 11 or 11 by 8½).
rules.why: Standardizes document layout across all submitted files and review systems.

rules.label: Use standard single-column text format

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: Proposers are strongly encouraged to use only a standard, single-column format for the text.
rules.why: Adhering to a single-column format ensures readability and consistent text layout across proposal documents.

rules.label: Ensure strict compliance with font and spacing rules to prevent return without review

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: consequently, the use of small fonts not in compliance with the above guidelines may be grounds for NSF to return the proposal without review.
rules.why: Proposals using non-compliant small fonts or line spacing violate fairness rules and are subject to immediate return without review.

rules.label: Enter LOI ID Number

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: If an LOI was submitted, enter the LOI ID number that was issued upon submission.
rules.why: It links the full proposal back to the previously submitted Letter of Intent.

rules.label: Provide Preliminary Proposal Number

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: If a preliminary proposal was submitted, and the organization was either invited or encouraged/discouraged to submit a full proposal, provide the Preliminary Proposal Number.
rules.why: It connects the full proposal submission to the corresponding preliminary proposal record.

rules.label: Provide Alternate Place of Performance Details

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: If the project will be performed at a location other than the awardee organization, provide the following information (where applicable).
rules.why: It notifies the reviewer and funding agency where project work will physically take place if outside the awardee organization.

rules.label: Identify Other Federal Agencies

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: If the proposal is being submitted for consideration by another Federal agency, the abbreviated name(s) of the Federal agency(ies) must be identified in the space provided.
rules.why: It discloses potential dual-submission or co-funding across federal agencies.

rules.label: Allow at least six months for NSF review in start date

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: The requested start date should allow at least six months for NSF review, processing, and decision.
rules.why: Proposing a start date with insufficient lead time can cause administrative processing issues and delay award processing.

rules.label: Provide physical location for research infrastructure projects

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: For research infrastructure projects, the project/performance site should correspond to the physical location of the asset.
rules.why: Accurate physical location reporting is required for proper oversight and auditing of infrastructure assets.

rules.label: Provide primary site or headquarters for distributed infrastructure

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: For research infrastructure that is mobile or geographically distributed, information for the primary site or organizational headquarters (as defined by the proposer) should be provided.
rules.why: NSF needs a designated primary physical hub or organizational base to track mobile or distributed infrastructure projects.

rules.label: Enter countries engaged with or traveled to for conferences

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: Proposers also should enter the country/countries with which project participants will engage and/or travel to attend international conferences.
rules.why: International travel and engagement require agency oversight and tracking.

rules.label: Enter Worldwide if specific international conference location unknown

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: If the specific location of the international conference is not known at the time of the proposal submission, proposers should enter “Worldwide”.
rules.why: Standardizes data entry on the Cover Sheet when specific foreign travel locations are not yet finalized.

rules.label: Write Project Summary to be informative and broadly understandable
rules.source: The Project Summary should be informative to other persons working in the same or related fields, and, insofar as possible, understandable to a broad audience within the scientific domain.
rules.why: Ensures the summary communicates the project effectively across different domain specialties.

rules.label: Do not frame Project Summary as a proposal abstract
rules.source: It should not be an abstract of the proposal.
rules.why: Ensures the summary is tailored as a standalone overview of activities and impacts rather than a standard abstract.

rules.label: State objectives and expected significance in Project Description
rules.source: The Project Description should provide a clear statement of the work to be undertaken and must include the objectives for the period of the proposed work and expected significance
rules.why: Reviewers need to evaluate the scope of work and its importance to the field.

rules.label: Describe relationship to present state of knowledge and PI's other work
rules.source: the relationship of this work to the present state of knowledge in the field, as well as to work in progress by the PI under other support.
rules.why: Reviewers must assess how the project builds on existing knowledge and connects to the PI's ongoing efforts.

rules.label: Outline general plan of work and experimental methods
rules.source: The Project Description should outline the general plan of work, including the broad design of activities to be undertaken, and, where appropriate, provide a clear description of experimental methods and procedures.
rules.why: Reviewers assess whether the technical design and methodology are feasible and rigorous.

rules.label: Justify foreign entity or international branch campus funding
rules.source: For proposals that include funding to an International Branch Campus of a U.S. IHE or to a foreign organization or foreign individual (including through use of a subaward or consultant arrangement), the proposer must provide the requisite explanation/justification in the project description.
rules.why: Reviewers and NSF need rationale for allocating funding to foreign entities or overseas campuses.

rules.label: Provide award number, amount, and period of support for prior NSF work
rules.source: (a) the NSF award number, amount and period of support;
rules.why: Reviewers require key administrative metadata to identify and contextualize prior awards.

rules.label: Provide project title for prior NSF support
rules.source: (b) the title of the project;
rules.why: Reviewers need the title of past funded projects to understand prior NSF investment.

rules.label: Describe prior results under separate Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts headings
rules.source: (c) a summary of the results of the completed work, including accomplishments, supported by the award. The results must be separately described under two distinct headings: Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts;
rules.why: Reviewers must assess prior contributions separately against the two NSF review criteria.

rules.label: List publications or explicitly state none were produced
rules.source: (d) a listing of the publications resulting from the NSF award (a complete bibliographic citation for each publication must be provided either in this section or in the References Cited section of the proposal); if none, state “No publications were produced under this award.”
rules.why: Reviewers require accurate reporting of prior research outputs or an explicit statement of no publications.

rules.label: Provide evidence of research products from prior NSF support
rules.source: (e) evidence of research products and their availability, including, but not limited to: data, publications, samples, physical collections, software, and models, as described in any Data Management and Sharing Plan; and
rules.why: Reviewers evaluate how well the PI shared data and research products from prior awards.

rules.label: Describe relation of completed work to proposed work for renewal proposals
rules.source: (f) if the proposal is for renewed support, a description of the relation of the completed work to the proposed work.
rules.why: Reviewers need to evaluate continuity and progress from the prior award into the new period.

rules.label: Describe goals and broader impacts if prior award has no new results
rules.source: If the project was recently awarded and therefore no new results exist, describe the major goals and broader impacts of the project.
rules.why: Reviewers need contextual information even when a project is too recent to have produced outcomes.

rules.label: Limit Results from Prior NSF Support to maximum five pages

check_args.handled_by: the page count of the file you upload — a paste has no pages

rules.source: Note that the proposal may contain up to five pages to describe the results.
rules.why: Reviewers need prior support results to fit within the designated length allocation.

rules.label: Describe unfunded substantial collaborations in Facilities section
rules.source: Any substantial collaboration with individuals not included in the budget should be described in the Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources section of the proposal (see Chapter II.D.2.g) and documented in a letter of collaboration from each collaborator.
rules.why: Reviewers evaluate collaborative support that does not involve direct budget requests.

rules.label: Provide collaboration letters in supplementary documentation
rules.source: Such letters should be provided in the supplementary documentation section of Research.gov and follow the format instructions specified in Chapter II.D.2.i.
rules.why: Reviewers require formal verification of committed collaborative assistance.

rules.label: Provide prior support report for most closely related award if multiple exist
rules.source: In cases where the PI or any co-PI has received more than one award (excluding amendments to existing awards), they need only report on the one award that is most closely related to the proposal.
rules.why: Clarifies which specific prior award must be documented when a investigator has received multiple NSF grants.

rules.label: Include author names in publication sequence
rules.source: Each reference must include the names of all authors (in the same sequence in which they appear in the publication), the article and journal title, book title, volume number, page numbers, and year of publication.
rules.why: Reviewers need complete and accurate bibliographic metadata to verify published sources.

rules.label: Include optional website URLs when available
rules.source: If the proposer has a website address readily available, that information should be included in the citation.
rules.why: Providing direct website addresses allows reviewers to quickly access cited materials.

rules.label: Restrict References Cited to bibliographic citations only
rules.source: While there is no established page limitation for the references, this section must include bibliographic citations only and must not be used to provide parenthetical information outside of the 15-page Project Description.
rules.why: Prevents applicants from circumventing the Project Description page limit by placing narrative text in the references section.

rules.label: Include complete publication metadata in references
rules.source: Each reference must include the names of all authors (in the same sequence in which they appear in the publication), the article and journal title, book title, volume number, page numbers, and year of publication.
rules.why: Missing core bibliographic elements prevents full verification and evaluation of the cited literature.

rules.label: Do not exceed page limits by using references for extra content
rules.source: this section must include bibliographic citations only and must not be used to provide parenthetical information outside of the 15-page Project Description.
rules.why: It prevents applicants from circumventing the 15-page Project Description limit by burying technical details in the references section.

rules.label: Include annual budget

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov budget form and the Budget Helper

rules.source: Each proposal must contain a budget for each year of support requested.
rules.why: Reviewers and NSF need to evaluate the financial feasibility of the proposed project for every requested year.

rules.label: Limit budget justification page count

check_args.handled_by: the page count of the file you upload — a paste has no pages

rules.source: The budget justification must be no more than five pages per proposal.
rules.why: Proposals exceeding page limits violate formatting rules and may be returned without review.

rules.label: Document and justify budget line items
rules.source: The amounts for each budget line item requested must be documented and justified in the budget justification as specified below.
rules.why: Reviewers rely on the justification to determine if requested amounts are necessary, reasonable, and allocable.

rules.label: Limit subaward budget justification page count

check_args.handled_by: the page count of the file you upload — a paste has no pages

rules.source: For proposals that contain a subaward(s), each subaward must include a separate budget justification of no more than five pages.
rules.why: Subaward documentation must adhere to the standard five-page maximum per subrecipient.

rules.label: Limit collaborative proposal budget justification page count

check_args.handled_by: the page count of the file you upload — a paste has no pages

rules.source: For collaborative proposals submitted by multiple organizations, each organization must include a separate budget justification of no more than five pages.
rules.why: Each collaborating organization must provide its own distinct budget justification within the specified page limit.

rules.label: Specify organizational definition of year in budget justification
rules.source: It is the organization’s responsibility to define and consistently apply the term “year”, and to specify this definition in the budget justification.
rules.why: Clarifies the timeframe applied when calculating senior personnel salary limits.

rules.label: Disclose and justify senior personnel salary exceeding two months
rules.source: If anticipated, any compensation for such personnel in excess of two months must be disclosed in the proposal budget, justified in the budget justification, and must be specifically approved by NSF in the award notice budget.
rules.why: Exceeding the standard two-month senior personnel salary limit requires explicit justification and agency approval.

rules.label: Match senior personnel person months with salary amount
rules.source: For consistency with the NSF cost sharing policy, if person months will be requested for senior/key personnel, a corresponding salary amount must be entered on the budget.
rules.why: Unfunded effort listed on the budget constitutes unallowable voluntary committed cost sharing.

rules.label: Remove unsalaried senior personnel from budget Section A

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov budget form and the Budget Helper

rules.source: If salary and person months are not being requested for an individual designated as a senior/key person, they should be removed from Section A of the budget.
rules.why: Prevents unallowable voluntary committed cost sharing from being included on the budget breakdown.

rules.label: List postdoctoral and professional personnel counts and rates
rules.source: For postdoctoral associates and other professionals, the total number of persons for each position must be listed, with the number of full-time-equivalent person-months and total amount of salaries requested per year.
rules.why: Provides transparency on the staffing level and budget requested for professional researchers.

rules.label: List student and secretarial counts and totals
rules.source: For graduate and undergraduate students, secretarial, clerical, technical, etc., whose time will be charged directly to the project, only the total number of persons and total amount of salaries requested per year in each category is required.
rules.why: Specifies the required budgeting granularity for non-senior project personnel.

rules.label: Detail pay rates in budget justification
rules.source: The budget justification should detail the rates of pay by individual for each senior/key person, postdoctoral associates, and other professionals.
rules.why: Allows reviewers to assess whether proposed individual compensation aligns with organizational practices and federal limits.

rules.label: Justify requested equipment
rules.source: Items of needed equipment must be adequately justified, listed individually by description and estimated cost.
rules.why: Reviewers must verify that requested equipment is necessary for project execution and unavailable otherwise.

rules.label: Disclose and justify special purpose computing equipment
rules.source: Any request to support such items must be clearly disclosed in the proposal budget, justified in the budget justification, and be included in the NSF award budget.
rules.why: General purpose computers are unallowable, so special scientific computing hardware must be explicitly justified.

rules.label: Itemize and justify travel details
rules.source: When anticipated, travel and its relation to the proposed activities must be specified, itemized, and justified by destination and cost.
rules.why: Ensures travel expenses directly support proposal objectives and follow federal cost principles.

rules.label: Include foreign travel destinations and dates on budget

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov budget form and the Budget Helper

rules.source: When anticipated, the proposer must enter the names of countries and dates of visit on the proposal budget, if known.
rules.why: Provides agency reviewers and program officers with specific foreign travel details.

rules.label: Justify non-standard participant support costs
rules.source: Any additional categories of participant support costs other than those described in 2 CFR § 200.1 (such as incentives, gifts, souvenirs, t-shirts, and memorabilia), must be justified in the budget justification, and such costs will be closely scrutinized by NSF.
rules.why: Ensures extra participant expenses are necessary and not unallowable promotional items.

rules.label: Specify participant count on budget

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov budget form and the Budget Helper

rules.source: The number of participants to be supported must be entered in the parentheses on the proposal budget.
rules.why: Establishes the scope of participant support requested on the official budget form.

rules.label: Itemize participant support in budget justification
rules.source: Participant support costs must be specified, itemized, and justified in the budget justification section of the proposal.
rules.why: Reviewers must evaluate the exact breakdown of participant stipends, travel, or subsistence.

rules.label: Detail materials and supplies in budget justification
rules.source: When anticipated, the proposal budget justification must indicate the general types of expendable materials and supplies required.
rules.why: Allows reviewers to confirm that requested supply items are directly applicable to the project.

rules.label: Justify requested computing devices
rules.source: Details and justification must be included for items requested to support the project.
rules.why: Direct charging of computing devices under $5,000 requires evidence of essential project need.

rules.label: Provide consultant details in budget justification
rules.source: Anticipated services must be justified, and information furnished on each individual’s expertise, primary organizational affiliation, normal daily compensation rate, and number of days of expected service.
rules.why: Reviewers must evaluate consultant qualification and confirm that daily pay rates are reasonable.

rules.label: Justify computer service rates
rules.source: A justification based on the established computer service rates at the proposing organization must be included.
rules.why: Confirms that requested computer service charges adhere to institutional rate policies.

rules.label: Disclose subaward arrangements in proposal
rules.source: If known at the time of proposal submission, the intent to enter into such arrangements must be disclosed in the proposal.
rules.why: NSF must grant authorization for any transfer of project work to subrecipients.

rules.label: Provide separate budget and justification for subrecipients
rules.source: A separate budget and a budget justification of no more than five pages, must be provided for each subrecipient, if already identified.
rules.why: Ensures proposed subaward costs are fully transparent and justified independently.

rules.label: Include subaward work description in Project Description
rules.source: The description of the work to be performed must be included in the project description.
rules.why: Reviewers must see how the subawardee's scope of work integrates into the overall research effort.

rules.label: Itemize Line G6 direct costs in budget justification
rules.source: Such costs must be itemized and detailed in the budget justification.
rules.why: Miscellaneous direct expenses require detailed explanation to prove allowability.

rules.label: Enter total direct costs on Line H

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov budget form and the Budget Helper

rules.source: The total amount of direct costs requested in the budget, to include Lines A through G, must be entered on Line H.
rules.why: Standardizes mathematical reporting of total direct expenses across all budget submissions.

rules.label: Specify indirect cost calculations in budget justification
rules.source: The amount for indirect costs must be calculated by applying the current negotiated indirect cost rate(s) to the approved base(s), and such amounts must be specified in the budget justification.
rules.why: Reviewers and officers must confirm that calculated F&A fees use valid rates and correct MTDC/direct bases.

rules.label: Enter total direct and indirect costs on Line J

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov budget form and the Budget Helper

rules.source: The total amount of direct and indirect costs (F&A) (sum of Lines H and I) must be entered on line J.
rules.why: Ensures correct arithmetic summary of total requested funds.

rules.label: Prohibit voluntary committed cost sharing
rules.source: Unless required by NSF (see the section on Mandatory Cost Sharing below), inclusion of voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited and Line M on the proposal budget will not be available for use by the proposer.
rules.why: NSF policy explicitly forbids unmandated voluntary committed cost sharing to maintain equity.

rules.label: Prohibit voluntary uncommitted cost sharing in budget
rules.source: As noted above, however, these resources are not auditable by NSF and should not be included in the proposal budget or budget justification.
rules.why: Prevents unquantified or non-auditable organizational contributions from contaminating official budget requests.

rules.label: Enter cumulative mandatory cost sharing on Year 1 budget Line M

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov budget form and the Budget Helper

rules.source: For purposes of budget preparation, the cumulative cost sharing amount must be entered on line M of the first year’s budget.
rules.why: Establishes the formal binding cost-sharing commitment required by programmatic rules.

rules.label: Justify entertainment costs in budget justification
rules.source: When costs typically considered as entertainment are necessary to accomplish the proposed objectives, they must be included in the budget and justified in the budget justification.
rules.why: Entertainment costs are normally unallowable and must be explicitly justified as necessary to project goals.

rules.label: Itemize and submit confidential senior personnel salary statement
rules.source: If this option is exercised, senior/key personnel salaries and person-months must be itemized in a separate statement and forwarded to NSF in accordance with the instructions specified in Chapter II.E.1.
rules.why: Ensures that detailed salary data for senior personnel is properly documented and submitted confidentially without exposing it to public reviewers.

rules.label: Provide explanation of mandatory cost sharing in budget justification
rules.source: An explanation of the source, nature, amount, and availability of any proposed cost sharing must be provided in the budget justification
rules.why: Validates that mandated cost-sharing commitments are backed by verifiable sources and available resources.
keywords: source and nature of cost sharing

rules.label: Do not request NSF funds for alcoholic beverages
rules.source: No NSF funds may be requested or spent for alcoholic beverages.
rules.why: Inclusion of unallowable costs like alcoholic beverages invalidates the proposal budget and violates federal funding guidelines.

rules.label: Do not request funds for home office workspace rental
rules.source: Rental of any property owned by individuals or entities affiliated with NSF recipients (including commercial or residential real estate), for use as home office workspace is unallowable.
rules.why: Requesting unallowable home office rental expenses creates a compliance violation in the project budget.

rules.label: Do not request funds for meals or coffee breaks for internal meetings
rules.source: No funds may be requested for meals or coffee breaks for intramural meetings of an organization or any of its components, including, but not limited to, laboratories, departments, and centers.
rules.why: Budgeting for internal meeting refreshments is strictly unallowable and must be excluded from the proposal budget.

rules.label: Do not request per diem or similar expenses for local participants
rules.source: funds may not be proposed to pay per diem or similar expenses for local participants in the conference.
rules.why: Paying per diem to local participants who are not in travel status is an unallowable cost under federal guidelines.

rules.label: Budget service agreement conference costs under Other Direct Costs
rules.source: Costs related to an NSF-sponsored conference (e.g., venue rental fees, catering costs, supplies, etc.) that will be secured through a service agreement/contract should be budgeted on line G.6., “Other Direct Costs” to ensure appropriate allocation of indirect costs.
rules.why: Categorizing service contracts properly ensures correct application of indirect cost rates.

rules.label: Do not budget incentive payments to research subjects under Participant Support
rules.source: This section of the budget also may not be used for incentive payments to research subjects.
rules.why: Participant support is strictly for trainees/participants, not human subjects, which require different indirect cost treatments.

rules.label: Include human subject payments under Line G.6 Other Direct Costs
rules.source: Human subject payments should be included on line G.6. of the NSF budget under “Other Direct Costs,” and any applicable indirect costs should be calculated on the payments in accordance with the organization’s Federally negotiated indirect cost rate.
rules.why: Human subject payments must be placed where indirect costs can be properly calculated.

rules.label: Do not include employee performance-based incentive payments under Line G.6
rules.source: Performance based incentive payments to employees as described in 2 CFR § 200.430(f) should not be included in this section of the budget.
rules.why: Employee incentive pay must be categorized under salaries and wages rather than general direct costs.

rules.label: Do not exceed mandatory cost sharing level specified in solicitation
rules.source: Proposers are advised not to exceed the mandatory cost sharing level or amount specified in the solicitation.
rules.why: Exceeding required cost sharing creates unallowable voluntary committed cost sharing.

rules.label: Do not count other Federal funds toward NSF cost sharing requirements
rules.source: contributions derived from other Federal funds or counted as cost sharing toward projects of another Federal agency must not be counted towards meeting the specific cost sharing requirements of the NSF award.
rules.why: Federal funds cannot be double-counted or used as matching for other federal awards.

rules.label: Describe directly applicable resources for review criteria
rules.source: This section of the proposal is used to assess the adequacy of the resources available to perform the effort proposed to satisfy both the Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts review criteria. Proposers should describe only those resources that are directly applicable.
rules.why: Reviewers need to assess whether the resources available are adequate to perform the proposed effort.

rules.label: Provide resource information exclusively in Facilities section
rules.source: Such information must be provided in this section, in lieu of other parts of the proposal (e.g., Budget Justification, Project Description).
rules.why: Placing resource descriptions in other sections violates structure rules and clutters other proposal components.

rules.label: Provide separate biographical sketch for each senior/key person via SciENcv

check_args.handled_by: SciENcv, which generates and formats these documents for you

rules.source: A biographical sketch must be provided separately for each individual designated as a senior/key person through use of SciENcv (Science Experts Network Curriculum Vitae).
rules.why: Reviewers need to assess the qualifications of each senior/key team member independently.

rules.label: Omit personal information from biographical sketch
rules.source: Individuals are reminded not to submit any personal information in the biographical sketch. This includes items such as: home address; home telephone, fax, or cell phone numbers; home e-mail address; driver’s license number; marital status; personal hobbies; and the like.
rules.why: Personal information is not relevant to the merits of the proposal and protects applicant privacy.

rules.label: Provide required identifying information in biographical sketch
rules.source: (1) Identifying Information (i) *Name: Enter the name of the senior/key person (Last name, First name, Middle name, including any applicable suffix). (ii) ORCID ID29 (Optional): Enter the ORCID ID of the senior/key person. (iii) *Position Title: Enter the current position title of the senior/key per
rules.why: Correctly identifies the senior/key individual associated with the biographical sketch.

rules.label: Provide organization and location in biographical sketch
rules.source: (2) *Organization and Location (i) Name: Enter the name of the primary organization of the senior/key person. (ii) Location: Enter the City, State/Province, and Country where the primary organization is located. If the State/Province is not applicable, enter N/A.
rules.why: Establishes the primary institutional affiliation of the individual.

rules.label: List professional preparation in reverse chronological order
rules.source: Provide a list of the senior/key person’s professional preparation (e.g., education and training), listed in reverse chronological order by start date. Include all postdoctoral and fellowship training, as applicable, listing each separately. Also include the baccalaureate degree or other initial pro
rules.why: Demonstrates the educational background and professional training history of the applicant.

rules.label: List appointments and positions in reverse chronological order
rules.source: Provide a list, in reverse chronological order by start date, of all the senior/key person’s academic, professional, or institutional appointments and positions, beginning with the current appointment (including the associated organization and location).
rules.why: Outlines the employment history and professional roles of the senior/key person.

rules.label: Limit external appointments and positions to a three-year window
rules.source: Senior/key personnel must only identify all domestic and foreign professional appointments and positions outside of the primary organization for a period of up to three years from the date the proposer submits the proposal to NSF for funding consideration.
rules.why: Restricts external position history to relevant recent activity.

rules.label: Provide required fields for each appointment entry
rules.source: For each entry provide: • Start date: YYYY • End date: YYYY • Appointment or Position Title • Name of organization • Department (if applicable) • Location of organization: City, State/Province, Country
rules.why: Ensures consistency and completeness for every listed professional position.

rules.label: Limit products list to ten specified items
rules.source: Provide a list of: (i) up to five products most closely related to the proposed project; and (ii) up to five other significant products, whether or not related to the proposed project that demonstrate the senior/key person’s qualifications to carry out the project.
rules.why: Evaluators rely on a concise, capped set of relevant publications or products to assess qualifications.

rules.label: Include required biographical certification language

check_args.handled_by: SciENcv, which generates and formats these documents for you

rules.source: I certify that the information provided is current, accurate, and complete. This includes but is not limited to information related to domestic and foreign appointments and positions. rules.why: Mandates formal confirmation of the accuracy of information and compliance with federal restrictions.

rules.label: Upload other personnel biographical information as a single PDF in Other Supplementary Documents

rules.source: The biographical information must be clearly identified as “Other Personnel” biographical information and uploaded as a single PDF file in the Other Supplementary Documents section of the proposal.
rules.why: Ensures non-key personnel qualifications are clearly grouped and submitted in the appropriate attachment area.

rules.label: Provide required biographical info and publication list for equipment proposal auxiliary users
rules.source: For equipment proposals, the following must be provided for each auxiliary user: (1) Short biographical sketch; and (2) List of up to five publications most closely related to the proposed acquisition.
rules.why: Allows reviewers to assess the need and qualifications of auxiliary users for equipment acquisition.

rules.label: Provide separate current and pending support for each senior/key person via SciENcv

check_args.handled_by: SciENcv, which generates and formats these documents for you

rules.source: Current and pending (other) support information must be provided separately for each individual designated as a senior/key person through use of SciENcv (Science Experts Network Curriculum Vitae).
rules.why: Allows evaluation of individual capacity, scientific overlap, and potential commitments.

rules.label: Disclose applicable consulting activities under proposals and active projects
rules.source: Consulting activities must be disclosed under the proposals and active projects section of the common form when any of the following scenarios apply: • The consulting activity will require the senior/key person to perform research as part of the consulting activity; • The consulting activity does no
rules.why: Ensures full transparency of consulting work that overlaps with or impacts research commitments.

rules.label: Omit personal information from current and pending support
rules.source: Individuals are reminded not to submit any personal information in the current and pending (other) support. This includes items such as: home address; home telephone, fax, or cell phone numbers; home e-mail address; driver’s license number; marital status; personal hobbies; and the like.
rules.why: Prevents improper inclusion of personal identifiers in scientific evaluation documents.

rules.label: Disclose all proposals and active projects with required details
rules.source: In this section, disclose ALL proposals and active projects in accordance with the definitions for current and pending (other) support.
rules.why: Ensures complete accounting of all active and pending research funding support.

rules.label: Limit overall objectives field in proposals/active projects to 1500 characters

rules.source: *Overall Objectives: Provide a brief statement of the overall objectives of the proposal/active project. This field is limited to 1500 characters.
rules.why: Enforces concise reporting of objectives for each listed support item.

rules.label: Describe potential scope, budget, or effort overlap in current/pending support
rules.source: *Statement of Potential Overlap: Enter a description of the potential overlap with any pending proposal or active foreign or domestic project and this proposal in terms of scope, budget, or person-months planned or devoted to the project by the individual. If there is no potential overlap, enter “no
rules.why: Prevents double-funding or conflicting commitments across funded projects.

rules.label: Disclose in-kind contributions valued at $5000 or more requiring time commitment
rules.source: In this section, disclose ALL in-kind contributions with an estimated dollar value of $5000 or more and that require a commitment of the individual’s time.
rules.why: Captures non-cash resource support that affects key personnel time and capacity.

rules.label: Limit overall objectives field in in-kind contributions to 1500 characters

check_args.handled_by: SciENcv, which generates and formats these documents for you

rules.source: *Overall Objectives: Provide a brief statement of the overall objectives of the in-kind contribution(s). This field is limited to 1500 characters.
rules.why: Enforces uniform reporting constraints across support entries.

rules.label: Include required certification in current and pending support

rules.source: I certify that the information provided is current, accurate, and complete. This includes, but is not limited to, information related to current, pending, and other support (both foreign and domestic) as defined in 42 U.S.C. § 6605. I also certify that, at the time of submission, I am not a party in
rules.why: Enforces mandatory legal certification regarding all foreign and domestic research support.

rules.label: Provide Collaborators & Other Affiliations information using the designated template

check_args.handled_by: SciENcv, which generates and formats these documents for you

rules.source: The COA information must be provided through use of the COA template. The information in the tables is not required to be sorted, alphabetically or otherwise.
rules.why: Standardizes information needed to identify and manage potential reviewer conflicts of interest.

rules.label: Do not alter COA template content, format, column sizes, or font type

check_args.handled_by: SciENcv, which generates and formats these documents for you

rules.source: The template has been developed to be fillable, however, the content and format requirements must not be altered by the user. When completing the template, do not change the column sizes or the font type.
rules.why: Ensures automated parsing and standard processing of conflict-of-interest data.

rules.label: Provide a maximum one-page document of up to five synergistic activities per senior/key person

rules.source: Each individual identified as a senior/key person must provide a document of up to one-page that includes a list of up to five distinct examples that demonstrates the broader impact of the individual’s professional and scholarly activities that focus on the integration and transfer of knowledge as w
rules.why: Allows reviewers to assess the individual's contributions to knowledge integration, transfer, and broader impacts within a set page limit.

rules.label: Ensure biographical sketch and support signatures are dated within 12 months

check_args.handled_by: SciENcv, which generates and formats these documents for you

rules.source: To be acceptable to NSF, the date of the signature must be within the past 12 months from when the document is submitted to the Foundation.
rules.why: It guarantees that the certification and disclosed support/biographical information are current at the time of proposal submission.

rules.label: Upload equipment proposal biographical information as a single PDF

check_args.handled_by: the formatting of the PDF you upload — check it there, not in the text

rules.source: Such information should be clearly identified as “Equipment Proposal” biographical information and uploaded as a single PDF file in the Other Supplementary Documents section of the proposal.
rules.why: It ensures auxiliary user qualifications for equipment proposals are properly packaged and located for evaluation.

rules.label: Convert foreign currency amounts to US dollars rounded to nearest dollar
rules.source: If the support is in a foreign country’s currency, convert to US dollars at time of submission.
rules.why: It standardizes financial values across proposals for consistent budgetary evaluation.

COA template Table 2: List names as last name, first nam
rules.why: It provides the specific reviewer conflict-of-interest data required by NSF to manage merit review selection.

rules.label: Identify other personnel biographical information clearly
rules.source: The biographical information must be clearly identified as “Other Personnel” biographical information and uploaded as a single PDF file in the Other Supplementary Documents section of the proposal.
rules.why: Ensures correct categorization and review of non-senior personnel qualifications.

rules.label: Identify equipment proposal biographical information clearly
rules.source: Such information should be clearly identified as “Equipment Proposal” biographical information and uploaded as a single PDF file in the Other Supplementary Documents section of the proposal.
rules.why: Ensures proper routing and review of auxiliary user qualifications in equipment proposals.

rules.label: Include all postdoctoral and fellowship training in professional preparation
rules.source: Include all postdoctoral and fellowship training, as applicable, listing each separately. Also include the baccalaureate degree or other initial professional education.
rules.why: Ensures the complete educational history required to evaluate key personnel qualifications is included in the proposal.

rules.label: Disclose foreign government-sponsored contracts and activities in support document
rules.source: Consistent with NSPM-33, senior/key personnel are required to disclose contracts associated with participation in programs sponsored by foreign governments, instrumentalities, or entities, including foreign government-sponsored talent recruitment programs.
rules.why: Verifies that foreign government support and potential conflicts of commitment are fully declared.

rules.label: Do not participate in a malign foreign talent recruitment program

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: In accordance with 42 U.S.C. § 19232, individuals are prohibited from being a party in a malign foreign talent recruitment program.
rules.why: Participation in malign foreign talent recruitment programs violates statutory requirements and disqualifies senior/key personnel.

rules.label: Enter N/A for non-applicable biographical sketch product citation fields

rules.source: If any of the items specified above is not applicable, enter N/A.
rules.why: Standardized entry of N/A prevents ambiguity in product citations during proposal review.

rules.label: Include Mentoring Plan for Postdocs or Graduate Students
rules.source: each proposal38 that requests funding to support postdoctoral scholars39 or graduate students must upload under “Mentoring Plan” in the supplementary documentation section of Research.gov, a description of the mentoring activities that will be provided for such individuals.
rules.why: Reviewers must evaluate the mentoring provided to supported postdocs and graduate students under the Broader Impacts criterion.

rules.label: Observe One-Page Limit for Mentoring Plan

check_args.handled_by: the page count of the file you upload — a paste has no pages

rules.source: In no more than one page, the mentoring plan must describe the mentoring that will be provided to all postdoctoral scholars or graduate students supported by the project, regardless of whether they reside at the submitting organization, any subrecipient organization, or at any organization participa
rules.why: Proposals must comply with established page limits for supplementary documentation.

rules.label: Do Not Use Mentoring Plan to Circumvent Project Description Limit
rules.source: Proposers are advised that the mentoring plan must not be used to circumvent the 15-page Project Description limitation.
rules.why: Supplementary documents cannot be used to extend the narrative of the main project description.

rules.label: Include Data Management and Sharing Plan
rules.source: Proposals must include a document of no more than two pages uploaded under “Data Management and Sharing Plan” in the supplementary documentation section of Research.gov.
rules.why: Reviewers evaluate how the proposal conforms to NSF policy on data dissemination and sharing.

rules.label: Limit Data Management and Sharing Plan to Two Pages

check_args.handled_by: the page count of the file you upload — a paste has no pages

rules.source: Proposals must include a document of no more than two pages uploaded under “Data Management and Sharing Plan” in the supplementary documentation section of Research.gov.
rules.why: Supplementary documents must adhere to specified length limits.

rules.label: Submit Single Unified Data Management Plan for Collaborative Projects
rules.source: Simultaneously submitted collaborative proposals and proposals that include subawards are a single unified project and should include only one supplemental combined Data Management and Sharing Plan, regardless of the number of non-lead collaborative proposals or subawards included.
rules.why: Collaborative proposals must present a single unified data strategy.

rules.label: Do Not Use Data Management Plan to Circumvent Project Description Limit
rules.source: Proposers are advised that the Data Management and Sharing Plan must not be used to circumvent the 15-page Project Description limitation.
rules.why: Supplementary documents cannot be used to bypass narrative length restrictions.

rules.label: Justify Data Management Plan Statement When No Data Is Produced
rules.source: A valid Data Management and Sharing Plan may include only the statement that no detailed plan is needed, for example, if no data, samples, physical collections, software, curriculum materials, or other materials are to be produced in the course of the project. However, such a statement must be accom
rules.why: Any omission of a full data plan must be formally justified to ensure compliance with sharing requirements.

rules.label: Restrict Letters of Collaboration Content
rules.source: Letters of collaboration should be limited to stating the intent to collaborate and should not contain endorsements or evaluation of the proposed project.
rules.why: Letters of collaboration must remain neutral commitment statements rather than promotional endorsements.

rules.label: Do Not Submit Unauthorized Letters of Support
rules.source: Proposals that contain letters of support not authorized by the program solicitation may be returned without review.
rules.why: Unsolicited or unauthorized letters of support violate agency rules and lead to administrative rejection.

rules.label: Include Logistical Plan for Antarctic Proposals
rules.source: Antarctic proposals to any NSF program require a “Logistical Requirements and Field Plan” supplementary document to be submitted with the proposal.
rules.why: Antarctic research requires explicit logistical planning for review and operational support.

rules.label: Obtain Tribal Permission for Research Impacting Tribal Interests
rules.source: If Tribal Nation resources or interests may be impacted by the proposed research, the proposer must follow the requirements set forth in Chapter II.E.10, related to seeking and obtaining permission from the potentially impacted Tribal Nation(s) in accordance with the directives of each Tribal Nation
rules.why: It ensures the proposal complies with required federal and tribal governance standards before conducting research that affects tribal lands or resources.

rules.label: Alert NSF to Proprietary, Privacy, or Security Circumstances
rules.source: In addition, the supplementary documentation section should alert NSF officials to unusual circumstances that require special handling, including, for example, proprietary or other privileged information in the proposal, matters affecting individual privacy or possible national security implications
rules.why: It notifies the agency of confidential or sensitive material in the submission that requires restricted handling during review.

rules.label: Upload Mentoring Plan under specified section in Research.gov

rules.source: each proposal38 that requests funding to support postdoctoral scholars39 or graduate students must upload under “Mentoring Plan” in the supplementary documentation section of Research.gov, a description of the mentoring activities that will be provided for such individuals.
rules.why: Verifies that the required plan is uploaded to the correct system location for automated checks and reviewer access.

rules.label: Describe mentoring activities for all supported postdocs and graduate students
rules.source: the mentoring plan must describe the mentoring that will be provided to all postdoctoral scholars or graduate students supported by the project, regardless of whether they reside at the submitting organization, any subrecipient organization, or at any organization participating in a simultaneously s
rules.why: Ensures all eligible project personnel receive required mentoring across all participating institutions.

rules.label: Submit a single unified mentoring plan for collaborative projects
rules.source: simultaneously submitted collaborative proposals, and collaborative proposals that include subawards, constitute a single unified project. Therefore, only one mentoring plan must be submitted for the entire project.
rules.why: Prevents redundant or conflicting mentoring plans from being submitted across collaborative project proposals.

rules.label: Upload Data Management Plan under specified supplementary section

check_args.handled_by: the Research.gov cover sheet, not a document you write

rules.source: Proposals must include a document of no more than two pages uploaded under “Data Management and Sharing Plan” in the supplementary documentation section of Research.gov.
rules.why: Ensures the document is correctly filed in the portal for review against data sharing policies.

rules.label: Discuss collaborative data issues within joint Data Management Plan
rules.source: In such collaborative proposals, the Data Management and Sharing Plan should discuss the relevant data issues in the context of the collaboration.
rules.why: Verifies that data governance, sharing, and access are explicitly addressed across all collaborating entities.

rules.label: Limit Letters of Collaboration to intent without endorsements
rules.source: Letters of collaboration should be limited to stating the intent to collaborate and should not contain endorsements or evaluation of the proposed project.
rules.why: Ensures collaboration letters remain objective commitments rather than unauthorized support letters.

rules.label: Ensure required Letters of Support are unique and author-approved
rules.source: A letter of support submitted in response to a program solicitation requirement must be unique to the specific proposal submitted and cannot be altered without the author’s explicit prior approval.
rules.why: Guarantees the authenticity and explicit consent of key stakeholders supporting the specific proposal.
